recap_lines: Bias is an offset from the truth, and more data does not move it.
Selection bias drops people, historical bias copies an unfair world.
Bias can sit in the sample, the labels or the structure.
Association watches a variable, intervention sets it.
Leverage analysis finds the path, the accountable owner controls it.
With unequal base rates, choosing a fairness metric is a values claim.
bookends.command: Quiz me on bias terms. Give me short cases, one at a time, about a data pipeline or a deployed model. For each, I must name the exact term, such as selection bias, sampling bias, historical bias, observer bias, label bias, structural bias, association, intervention, leverage or accountable owner, and say why its look-alike is wrong. Do not reveal the answer until I reply. Then correct me.

beats.narration_text: Here is a percent line. Each dot is one estimate from one sample, in a simulated run. An estimator is the recipe that turns a sample into a number. An unbiased estimator can miss on any one sample, but its dots gather around the truth, the red dashed line at twenty-five percent. For example, an agent averages the pay in a random batch of data analyst listings. That average is an estimator. One batch may miss, but the batches center on the true pay, so it is unbiased.

Chance alone gives zero point five, so kappa is zero point six. For example, two recruiters each mark the same résumés as qualified or not. Kappa asks how far their agreement goes beyond what two people guessing at their own rates would reach by luck.
